Thought: I will manually calculate the moles of NaOH using the given concentration and volume, then determine the moles of acid neutralized.

Calculation:

1. Convert the volume of NaOH from cm³ to dm³:
   \[
   19.40 \, \text{cm}^3 = 19.40 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{dm}^3 = 0.0194 \, \text{dm}^3
   \]

2. Calculate the moles of NaOH:
   \[
   \text{Moles of NaOH} = \text{Concentration} \times \text{Volume} = 0.100 \, \text{mol dm}^{-3} \times 0.0194 \, \text{dm}^3 = 0.00194 \, \text{mol}
   \]

Since each mole of NaOH neutralizes one mole of acid, the moles of acid in the sample are equal to the moles of NaOH.
